metadata.description: Flash-only reasoning-effort routing for DeepSeek Harness, setting the DeepSeek flash model reasoning effort per step. The model never changes; effort max is opt-in.

# dsh-model-router
English | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps a pool of
models and routes every step to one of them with its

reasoning effort set. Thinking stays on —
DeepSeek rejects a thinking-enabled request whose history

contains a tool call made with thinking
off.
## Routing table
| Step class | Decided by | Reasoning effort | Internal point |

| `trivial` | a clearly cheap intent (translate, rename, reformat) in a short step | `low` | ~50 |
|

`standard` | a plain short request with no engineering cue | `low` | ~50 |
| `engineering` | engine

ering cues, code/diff/XML structure, or an agent tool loop | `high` | ~75 |
| `hard` | a dense engin
eering brief, or failures earned inside the task | `high` (`max` when `allowMax`) | ~75 / 100 |

`high` is the default ceiling. V4.1-Flash drives effort from an internal 1–100 scalar and exposes
th

ree preset names; `high` corresponds to roughly 75, which is where the published effort curve is
sti
ll steep. Pushing past it costs about 1.6–1.8x the output tokens for a marginal gain.
Since v0.15.0 `routes.<class>.effort` accepts any of the nine effort words (`off`, `none`, `minimal`
, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `ultra`); a target that does not know a word gets the nea
rest tier, breaking ties upward (quality first). `off` and the max-class words still go through rule
g ties upward (quality first). `off` and the max-class words still go through rule 5 and `allowMax`.
## Authorization scopes, the model pool and task presets (v0.5)
`control` decides what the router owns, and a manual pick only counts in the scope that owns it: an

effort change stands down `full`/`effort` but not `model`, and a model switch stands down
`full`/`mo

del` but not `effort`. While the router is down it stays out until the next command or the
composer
control's **resume** action.
| Scope | Owns |

| `full` — 模型+思考 / Model+Effort | model + reasoning effort |
[该节后续省略]
## What 1.0.0 actually promises (v1.0.0)

A 1.0 is a promise about what will not break, so this version is mostly about making the existing
su
rface legible rather than adding capability.
- **A versioned envelope.** Every HTTP response from the panel's router — including the 403, 405 and

400 answers produced by the transport — now carries `"schemaVersion": 1`. A reader can refuse an
en

velope it does not understand instead of guessing; `docs/api.md` documents the sixteen routes and
th

e module entry points published through `package.json#exports`.
- **The contract is tested, not just

described.** `test/contract.test.js` fails if `docs/api.md` and
the registered routes disagree, if

a host event the plugin listens to is missing from
`docs/compat.md`, if an export stops resolving or

escapes the published directories, or if a
response ever loses its `schemaVersion`.
- **Degradation

is named.** `/state.compat` reports `missing` (a capability without which routing
cannot run, today

only `sessionProjections`) and `optional` (`webServer`, `commands`, `llm`). The
panel renders a not

e listing what is missing in the chat language, so a host that is too old shows
as a shortcoming ins

tead of looking fine while features silently do nothing.
- **An upgrade path with no migration.** `d

ocs/migration-0.14-to-1.0.md` lists every configuration key
added since 0.14.2, notes that nothing n

eeds migrating (the state file is read as-is), and records
the one default that changed shape: `peak

Policy` starts at `inform`, which only ever prints.
- **Additive within 1.x.** Modules may gain expo

rts and `/state` may gain fields in a minor release;
removing or repurposing either waits for 2.0. `

PUBLISHING.md` covers the mechanics, `CONTRIBUTING.md`
the checks a change must pass, and `SECURITY.
md` what the plugin stores and what it never reads.
Deliberately not in this version: splitting the browser bundle into a build artifact, and a CI matri

x
against two host versions. Both are infrastructure work that does not change what the router decid

es,
and both are recorded as deferred in `PLAN.md` rather than implied by the version number.
## Requirements and compatibility

- Node 20 or newer.
- `engines.dsh` is declared as `>=0.1.7-rc.2 <0.2.0`; tested on `@deepseek-ai/ds

h` 0.1.7-rc.2.
The plugin uses `agent/request`, `agent/inbox/claimed`, `session.deriveMessages()` an

d the
session projections (`modelSelection`, `todos`, `contextPressure`, `tokenUsage`).
- **Do not**

declare `@deepseek-ai/*` `peerDependencies` in the plugin root. The host boot gate only
reads peerD

ependencies and silently skips a plugin it cannot resolve instead of failing; `engines.dsh`
is used

by dshmarket for install-time compatibility only and does not affect boot. The runtime
defence is th

e startup self-check planned for 0.15+ (a missing contract switches to degraded and
says so in the p

anel).
- Only the web composer seat (`conversation.input.model`) is verified; when the host does not

declare
that seat the panel falls back to the `conversation.input.right` chip.
## Limitations
- **No config schema.** Settings are read from the profile patch layer shown above and do not render

as a form in the settings UI. This is deliberate: a schema would require importing
`@deepseek-ai/*`

packages, which a plugin installed beside the profile cannot resolve.
- The router only touches the

`deepseek-official` provider and models matching `familyPattern`.
- **The router control takes over

the official model cell by registration, not by patching the
component.** It registers into `conver

sation.input.model` at priority -1 (below the shipped
`ModelSelect` at 0), keeping the official mode

l + effort sections inside its own panel. The old
`conversation.input.right` chip (`model-router:com

poser-control`, order 20) self-retracts and is only
a fallback for a host that rejects the seat. 0.1

0.0's first attempt shipped a blank cell and was
rolled back in 0.10.1 because it had not declared `

sessions` / `remote` / `remote.session` on the
plugin root.
- **The per-call route line is a separat

e small row** anchored after the tool call, not a badge inside
the harness's own tool row or inside

the thinking chain: a keyed slot replaces whatever it targets,
and the thinking chain exposes no chi

ld slot. A call the host has not folded yet shows nothing
rather than guessing. Plugin source change
s only appear after you restart `dsh web`.
